idea_name: Kaufman AMA Efficiency-Ratio adaptive MA as volatility-aware trend sensor
mechanism: Compute AMA/KAMA via Efficiency Ratio ER = net price change / sum of absolute bar changes over ama_period, map ER into smoothing constant SC between fast and slow EMA periods, then AMA_t = AMA_{t-1} + SC*(price_t - AMA_{t-1}). Fire buy when close crosses above AMA (prev close below), sell on cross below. AMA lengthens in chop (low ER) and shortens in trend (high ER), so the same crossover rule becomes a volatility-conditioned regime/turning-point sensor.
data_needed: OHLC closes; ama_period, fast_ma_period, slow_ma_period; bar-close events
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; H1; 2022-01-01 to 2022-06-30; lot=1; MAPeriod=50, fast=5, slow=100
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a built-in adaptive smoother whose lag self-tunes to efficiency of price path—usable as a regime label (trending vs noisy) and change sensor without a separate vol estimator.
quote: The main concept is to reduce the noise in the price movement. It follows the price movement whatever the volatility of this price movement as it adjusts to it. The indicator is a trend-follower indicator, so, it can be used to identify the trend and the turning points.

idea_name: Fixed-period MA-family crossover battery (SMA/DEMA/TEMA/FrAMA vs AMA)
mechanism: Run identical close-cross rules on SMA, DEMA=(2*EMA1)-EMA2, TEMA=(3*EMA1)-(3*EMA2)+EMA3, FrAMA (Ehlers fractal dimension adaptive), and AMA under fixed H1/50 settings; rank by net profit, DD, PF, Sharpe. On the tested window AMA dominates (PF 1.31, Sharpe 0.86) while DEMA/TEMA/FrAMA lose—so relative performance of lag-reduced vs adaptive MAs itself senses whether the market is smooth-trend or fractal-choppy.
data_needed: Same OHLC window for each iMA/iAMA/iDEMA/iTEMA/iFrAMA handle; Strategy Tester metrics
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; Jan–Jun 2022; period 50 across types
why_new_for_mis: Treats the spread of outcomes across MA lag profiles as a market-structure sensor: when adaptive AMA wins and multi-EMA lag killers fail, MIS can flag a noise-dominated regime.
quote: According to the results of all our tests, we have two types that have the best performance based on the settings and tested period. These are the simple moving average and the adaptive moving average. The best one is the adaptive moving average.

idea_name: OnTradeTransaction ArrayPrint log of NETTING volume/avg-price lifecycle
mechanism: Instrument OnTradeTransaction to dump MqlTradeTransaction/Request/Result via ArrayPrint while opening, adding, and closing a NETTING position (WDOU23). Parse type sequence TRADE_TRANSACTION_ORDER_ADD → DEAL_ADD → ORDER_DELETE → HISTORY_ADD → REQUEST; use DEAL_ADD (type 6) with stable position ticket to detect avg-price/volume change without polling PositionsTotal—required because replay/simulation cannot rely on server position APIs.
data_needed: Live or demo OnTradeTransaction stream; deal/order/position ticket fields; account type (NETTING vs HEDGING)
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: WDO$ / WDOU23 (B3 mini dollar futures); M30 chart in log; Chart Trade + EA
why_new_for_mis: Event-driven fill/position-state sensor that tracks when average entry and volume actually change—usable by MIS as a microstructure/position-regime feed and as a template for replay-faithful state machines.
quote: The simplest solution is to use the OnTradeTransaction function to solve our problem, because it is called only when something happens. The server reports exactly what happened, so there is no need for us to figure it out ourselves.

idea_name: Bootstrap confidence intervals on annualized mean returns (pivot/percentile/BCA)
mechanism: From an OOS returns series, draw nboot resamples with replacement; compute test statistic MeanReturns (mean return annualized by TF: *252 D1, *52 W1, *12 MN1, else scale by PeriodSeconds). Form CI via pivot, percentile, or bias-corrected-and-accelerated (jackknife acceleration) methods at user probabilities (e.g. 0.9/0.95/0.975). Lower bound is a worst-case expected-return sensor for go/no-go; inspect bootstrap distribution for heavy tails before trusting ratio metrics.
data_needed: Out-of-sample returns array (saved from tester); nboot≥1000; confidence probabilities; optional GetBootStrapStatistics plot
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: MovingAverage_Demo EA; EURUSD (script example D1); returns types ALL_BARS / POSITION_OPEN_BARS / TRADES
why_new_for_mis: Turns single-run tester profit into a probability-bounded forward-performance sensor MIS can gate strategy promotion on, instead of raw Sharpe or point net profit.
quote: What they do is provide methods to identify strategies with a high probability of producing significant or acceptable profit.

idea_name: Multi-granularity equity-returns collectors for CI inputs
mechanism: CReturns OnNewTick accumulates three parallel equity curves: every bar, only bars with an open position, and completed-trade equity; GetReturns differences them into return series selectable via ENUM_RETURNS_TYPE. Choice of granularity changes the bootstrap CI and thus the sensed risk of the same strategy path.
data_needed: Tick/bar equity path in tester or live; deal history for TRADES mode
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol under test; MA demo EA; configurable return_type input
why_new_for_mis: Lets MIS sense whether edge exists only while in market vs on idle bars—avoids optimistic all-bars return inflation when building performance CIs.
quote: ENUM_RETURNS_ALL_BARS defines a series of bar by bar returns for all bars of a test period. ENUM_RETURNS_POSITION_OPEN_BARS is series of returns that constitutes the bar by bar returns for those bars a position was open. ENUM_RETURNS_TRADES defines a returns series of completed trades only.

mechanism: Physics-inspired metaheuristic (Coulomb charge spheres, velocity+acceleration updates) for black-box parameter search on Rastrigin/Forest/Megacity benches. Optimizer for EA tuning, not a market sensor.

idea_name: Rolling-close RandomForest regressor with RobustScaler+PolynomialFeatures pipeline
mechanism: Label each bar with a near-future close; build feature vectors of the last n_steps=100 closes; Pipeline(MinMaxScaler → RobustScaler → PolynomialFeatures → RandomForestRegressor) trains and exports to ONNX. MT5 EA feeds last 100 closes into OnnxRun and maps predicted vs current close to PRICE_UP/DOWN/SAME (optionally gated by tight spread).
data_needed: EURUSD H1 closes from 2000–2023; n_steps window; trained rf_pipeline.onnx; optional spread filter
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; H1; SAMPLE_SIZE=100; TP/SL inputs in EA
why_new_for_mis: Sequence→tabular RF with robust/polynomial preprocessing as a deployable next-price neural/tree sensor inside the terminal via ONNX.
quote: As you can see, a pipeline is a sequence of data processing and modeling steps combined into one chain. ... PolynomialFeatures applies a polynomial transformation to the features. This adds polynomial features that can help the model account for nonlinear relationships in the data.

mechanism: Opens initial buy/sell then doubles lot every `distance` pips against the move; closes whole basket when price reaches volume-weighted average ± takeProfit. Execution/MM strategy, not a market regime sensor.

idea_name: GRU (vs LSTM) sequential close forecast to ONNX EA
mechanism: Pull EURUSD H1 rates; StandardScaler on features/target; train dense/GRU-style stack (L2, Dropout, EarlyStopping, ReduceLROnPlateau, optional KFold windows) with Adam+MSE; export ONNX; EA runs inference for next-price direction. Side-by-side LSTM (Conv1D+LSTM) comparison shows similar accuracy with GRU faster—select cell type by compute budget.
data_needed: EURUSD H1 OHLCV; train/val split (e.g. 80/20 chronological); ONNX model in MQL5 Files; scaler params at inference
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; TIMEFRAME_H1; January 2024 backtest example; window_size/days configurable
why_new_for_mis: Production path for a recurrent sequence price sensor in MIS: train in Python, gate in MT5 via ONNX, with explicit GRU-vs-LSTM speed/expressivity tradeoff.
quote: GRU emerges as a favored alternative to LSTM for sequential data modeling, particularly in scenarios where computational constraints exist or a simpler architecture is preferred.
